paragraphs: A new plaque is now on a house in Dublin. It remembers the writer John McGahern. The Lord Mayor of Dublin, Daryl Barron, put it up on Saturday morning.
The house is at 57 Howth Road in Clontarf. McGahern lived there in the 1960s. He wrote his first two books in a room upstairs. They were The Barracks and The Dark.
In 1965, the government banned The Dark. After that, McGahern lost his job as a teacher at a local school.

A professor, Frank Shovlin, had the idea for the plaque. He wrote to the owners of the house, and they said yes. McGahern died in 2006. Dublin City Council only puts up a plaque 20 years after a person dies.
sentZh: 一塊新的紀念牌現在掛在都柏林的一棟房子上。
它紀念作家約翰．麥加恩。
都柏林市長達瑞爾．巴倫在星期六早上把它掛上去。
這棟房子位於克朗塔夫的霍斯路57號。
麥加恩在1960年代住在那裡。
他在樓上的一個房間寫了他的頭兩本書。
那兩本書是《營房》和《黑暗》。
1965年，政府查禁了《黑暗》。
在那之後，麥加恩失去了在當地一所學校當老師的工作。
一位教授法蘭克．肖夫林想出了掛紀念牌的點子。
他寫信給屋主，他們答應了。
麥加恩於2006年去世。
都柏林市議會只在一個人去世20年後才會掛上紀念牌。

paragraphs: A plaque in memory of the Irish writer John McGahern was unveiled on Saturday morning at a house in Clontarf, Dublin. The Lord Mayor of Dublin, Daryl Barron, unveiled it at 57 Howth Road.

McGahern is mostly connected with the countryside of Leitrim and north Roscommon, where he grew up. However, he wrote his first two novels, The Barracks (1963) and The Dark (1965), in an upstairs room of this Dublin house.
He was still living there in 1965 when The Dark was banned. Soon after, he lost his job as a teacher at Belgrove National School in Clontarf.

The idea came from Frank Shovlin, a professor of Irish literature at the University of Liverpool, who has studied McGahern for about 20 years. He wrote to the owners, Una and Robert Mullins, and they agreed.

Councillor Donna Cooney said the plaque helps to make up for how the State treated the writer. Mr Barron said McGahern's subjects, such as violence at home and the failure to protect children, are still important today. McGahern died in March 2006, and the council waits at least 20 years after a death before putting up a plaque.
sentZh: 星期六早上，一塊紀念愛爾蘭作家約翰．麥加恩的牌匾在都柏林克朗塔夫的一棟房子揭幕。
都柏林市長達瑞爾．巴倫在霍斯路57號為它揭幕。
麥加恩大多與他成長的利特里姆郡和北羅斯康芒郡的鄉村連結在一起。
不過，他是在這棟都柏林房子的樓上房間寫下他的頭兩部小說《營房》（1963）和《黑暗》（1965）。
1965年《黑暗》被查禁時，他仍住在那裡。
不久之後，他失去了在克朗塔夫貝爾格羅夫國小的教職。
這個點子來自利物浦大學愛爾蘭文學教授法蘭克．肖夫林，他研究麥加恩已約20年。
他寫信給屋主烏娜和羅伯特．穆林斯，他們同意了。
市議員唐娜．庫尼說，這塊牌匾有助於彌補國家當年對這位作家的對待。
巴倫先生說，麥加恩寫的主題，例如家庭暴力和未能保護兒童，至今仍然重要。
麥加恩於2006年3月去世，而市議會會在一個人去世至少20年後才掛上牌匾。

paragraphs: A commemorative plaque honouring the novelist John McGahern was unveiled on Saturday morning at 57 Howth Road in Clontarf, Dublin, by the Lord Mayor, Cllr Daryl Barron.

Although McGahern is mainly associated with rural Leitrim and north Roscommon, where he was raised, he wrote his first two novels, The Barracks (1963) and The Dark (1965), in an upstairs room of the house. He was still living there when The Dark was banned in 1965, and he was subsequently dismissed from his teaching post at Belgrove National School nearby.
